**The document doesn't report an average treatment effect or p-value for a short-term homepage engagement metric.** It never names a "homepage engagement" metric, and it gives no p-values for any online metric.

The paper says this about the online A/B test:

- **Setup:** It ran on about 10% of Netflix traffic for 4 weeks, on key batch-compute surfaces (p. 6).
- **Short- and long-term metrics:** Under a low-data, low-signals configuration, the Phase-2 GenRec model showed "statistically significant improvement over the production baseline on both short-term and long-term online metrics," with a pointer to Figure 3 (p. 6).
- **Only number given:** There was a "+0.006% relative improvement on our core online metric," described as "statistically meaningful at Netflix scale" (p. 6). The paper doesn't say whether this core metric is short-term, long-term, or homepage-related.

Figure 3 ("Online metrics of GenRec vs. production model," p. 6) may contain per-metric results. However, it appears only as an image here, and its values aren't in the text, so I can't read effect sizes or p-values from it.
